text:
The lanterns' glow painted Julian's shoulders in shifting gold, the light pooling in the hollow beneath his throat. I shouldered past him before his name could catch in my teeth, the parchment crumpling against my hip like a second heartbeat. My cloak snagged on the rough stone of the alley's mouth, the fabric's edge fraying between restless fingers. The wind that followed us down the narrow way carried the scent of distant blush and damp moss, and then—suddenly—the enchanted lanterns along the wall guttered out one by one, their flickering light swallowed by the dark.

Julian's arm shot out, bracing against the alley wall before I could stumble into the void where the glow had been. His fingers grazed my waist, just the barest pressure, but it was enough to make my breath stutter. "You're not thinking straight," he said, voice low enough that the words might have been meant only for the stones beneath our boots. His shadow stretched long and sharp across the wet cobblestones, a silhouette of someone who had long since learned how to stand between a person and their own poor judgment.

I twisted my wrist free from his hold, the motion small but decisive. "What straight path is there?" The lanterns had been our only light, and now the alley had folded inward around us, the darkness thick enough to taste. My pulse thrummed in the hollow of my throat, where his eyes had lingered earlier tonight—not with heat, but with something quieter, something that had settled beneath my skin and refused to be scratched out.

His ring finger tapped once against his thigh, the rhythm steady as a metronome counting down to something irreversible. "There's always a path," he answered, stepping closer until the heat of him pressed against the chill seeping through my clothes. His gaze tracked the movement of my hands, as if the way I worried the frayed edge of my cloak held the key to an answer he'd spent half his life seeking.

A gust of wind tore through the alley again, colder this time, and the last lantern sputtered back to life—just in time to catch the silhouette of someone standing at the far end of the passage. Tall. Still. Watching.
